newsitem.title: UK: Ulster TV seeks real growth in ad revenue.
newsitem.headline: Ulster TV seeks real growth in ad revenue.

text.p: Regional broadcaster Ulster TV Plc said on Monday it was "cautiously optimistic" of seeing a return to real growth in advertising revenues this year.
"After a reasonably good start to the year we are cautiously optimistic, and expect a return to some real growth (that is, above inflation) for the year," chairman John McGuckian said in a statement.
Ulster TV reported 1996 pre-tax profit of 9.0 million stg, up from 8.2 million in 1995. Advertising revenue grew by only 2.4 percent, in line with inflation, to 33.2 million stg.
Ulster said its viewing share of 42 percent was the highest in the ITV network of regional broadcasters and compared with ITV's overall share of 35 percent.
However, it said it had been penalised by the method by which advertisers buy airtime in the ITV network.

Under the "equal impact" buying system, advertisers seek to reach an equal number of viewers in the various ITV regions. Less airtime is needed to reach the same number of people in high viewing areas such as Ulster.
Ulster Managing Director Desmond Symth said he did not expect a big impact this year from the launch of Channel 5.
